name: rpk-security skill vs docs
description: Measures whether the rpk-security skill adds value over the published docs for rpk security (users, ACLs, roles, secrets) and the security properties it covers. Sampled and targeted cases were picked from the full rpk-security skill, before it was converted to the thin format, and from the public redpanda source at tag v26.2.2, without regard to the docs. Behavioral cases grade the outcome of a task run against a mocked rpk: revoking one operation without removing others, offboarding a user's ACLs and role membership, adding a superuser without dropping the existing ones, changing a Cloud secret's scopes without overwriting its value, and rotating a password without changing its SCRAM mechanism. The shell mock is stateless, so the invariants do not fail an answer for reporting that a listing after a change still shows the old state.

test_cases.query: On my self-managed Redpanda cluster I ran `rpk cluster config set enable_sasl true` and never touched kafka_enable_authorization. Are ACLs being enforced on Kafka clients right now, or is authorization still off until I set that property too?
test_cases.why: kafka_enable_authorization is nullable and defaults to null. While it is null, authorization follows enable_sasl, so turning on SASL also enforces ACLs. Set to true or false, it overrides enable_sasl. A model that assumes the property defaults to false says ACLs are not enforced.
verified_against: redpanda src/v/config/configuration.cc, kafka_enable_authorization (std::nullopt default, null follows enable_sasl) (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: acls_enforced_via_null
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says ACLs are not enforced, or that authorization stays off until kafka_enable_authorization is set to true. Passes if it says ACLs are enforced, because kafka_enable_authorization is unset (null) by default and then follows enable_sasl.

test_cases.query: Last month I removed SASL user bob with `rpk security user delete bob`. Today a new hire, also named bob, needs a SCRAM account on the same Redpanda cluster. If I create user bob again, what access will the new account have on day one?
test_cases.why: rpk security user delete removes only the SCRAM credential; ACLs for User:bob stay in the ACL store, so a new user with the same name inherits them at once. A model that assumes Kafka-style cleanup says the new account starts with no access.
verified_against: redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/user/delete.go long help: 'This does not delete any ACLs that may exist for this user' (tag v26.2.2)
redpanda src/v/redpanda/admin/security.cc delete_user_handler (credential only) (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: inherits_old_acls
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the new bob starts with no permissions, or that deleting the user removed its ACLs. Passes if it says the old ACLs for User:bob still exist and apply to the new account, so it gets the old bob's access unless those ACLs are deleted first.

test_cases.query: User alice has three ACLs on topic orders: allow read, allow write, and allow describe. If I run `rpk security acl delete --allow-principal alice --topic orders --no-confirm`, which of those three does it remove?
test_cases.why: rpk security acl delete works on filters, and any flag left out matches everything, so without --operation the delete removes all three ACLs, not only one. --no-confirm skips the preview prompt that would have listed them.
verified_against: redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/acl/delete.go long help: 'Any unspecified flag defaults to matching everything' (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: all_three_removed
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says only some of the ACLs are removed, that the command errors because no operation was given, or that it asks which one. Passes if it says all three (read, write and describe) are removed, because an unspecified operation matches every operation.

test_cases.query: If I delete a Redpanda RBAC role with `rpk security role delete analysts --no-confirm`, what happens to the ACLs bound to that role and to the users assigned to it?
test_cases.why: Deleting a role removes every ACL bound to it (principal RedpandaRole:<name>) and unassigns its members. A model that reasons from Kafka ACL behavior may say the role's ACLs remain orphaned in the ACL store.
verified_against: redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/role/delete.go long help: 'This action will remove all associated ACLs from the role and unassign members' and DeleteRole(..., deleteACLs=true) (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: acls_and_members_removed
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the role's ACLs stay behind or must be deleted separately, or that the users keep the role's permissions. Passes if it says the ACLs bound to the role are deleted and the members are unassigned. Mentioning that the users themselves are not deleted is fine.

test_cases.query: I want to store a database password as a Redpanda Cloud secret named db-password, using `rpk security secret create --name db-password --value ... --scopes redpanda_connect`. Will rpk accept that name? If not, what name rules do I need to follow?
test_cases.why: rpk validates secret names before sending: they must start with an uppercase letter and contain only uppercase letters, digits, and underscores, up to 255 characters. db-password fails on both case and the hyphen.
verified_against: redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/secret/secret.go validateSecretName (^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$, max 255) (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: rejects_name_with_rule
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says db-password is accepted, or that rpk uppercases it automatically, or gives a rule that allows lowercase letters or hyphens. Passes if it says the name is rejected and that a name must start with an uppercase letter and use only uppercase letters, digits and underscores (for example DB_PASSWORD).

test_cases.query: Our Redpanda cluster accepts OIDC tokens on its Kafka listener. I already have an access token from our identity provider in $TOKEN. How do I make rpk itself authenticate with that token when I run `rpk topic list`?
test_cases.why: rpk supports SASL/OAUTHBEARER for the Kafka API: set sasl.mechanism to OAUTHBEARER and pass the token in the pass field, optionally prefixed with token:. There is no separate token flag, so a model that guesses invents one.
verified_against: redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/config/params.go, sasl.mechanism help ('For OAUTHBEARER, pass the token via the pass field (optionally prefixed with "token:")') (tag v26.2.2)
redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/kafka/client_franz.go OAUTHBEARER branch (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: token_in_pass_field
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer tells the user to pass the token through a flag or setting other than the SASL password (pass) field, or says rpk cannot authenticate with OIDC tokens. Passes if it sets sasl.mechanism=OAUTHBEARER and puts the token in pass (for example -X pass=token:$TOKEN or -X pass=$TOKEN), on the command line or in a profile.

test_cases.query: Audit logging has been on for months on our self-managed Redpanda cluster and _redpanda.audit_log has 12 partitions. If I now run `rpk cluster config set audit_log_num_partitions 24`, does the audit topic get 24 partitions?
test_cases.why: audit_log_num_partitions (and audit_log_replication_factor) apply only when Redpanda creates the audit topic; they cannot change an existing audit log topic. So they must be set before audit logging is first enabled.
verified_against: redpanda src/v/config/configuration.cc, audit_log_num_partitions: 'Defines the number of partitions used by a newly-created audit topic ... This cannot be altered for existing audit log topics.' (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: no_effect_on_existing_topic
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the existing audit topic grows to 24 partitions, or that the change applies after a restart or a toggle of audit_enabled without recreating the topic. Passes if it says the setting only applies to a newly created audit topic and does not change the existing one.

test_cases.query: How do I turn on FIPS mode on the brokers of my self-managed Redpanda cluster with rpk?
test_cases.why: fips_mode is a broker (node) property in redpanda.yaml, not a cluster property, so it is set per broker with rpk redpanda config set redpanda.fips_mode (or in redpanda.yaml) and the broker restarted. rpk cluster config set fips_mode is the common wrong guess.
verified_against: redpanda src/v/config/node_config.cc fips_mode (tag v26.2.2)
redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/redpanda/config.go (rpk redpanda config set) (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: per_broker_setting
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer sets fips_mode as a cluster property (rpk cluster config set) or says one command applies it to the whole cluster. Passes if it sets fips_mode per broker in redpanda.yaml, for example with rpk redpanda config set redpanda.fips_mode enabled, on each broker.

test_cases.query: We use OIDC with Keycloak, and the token's groups claim has path-style values like /engineering/platform. I created an ACL for principal Group:platform, but it never matches. What do I change on the Redpanda side so that ACL matches?
test_cases.why: The nested_group_behavior cluster property controls path-style group names: none (default) keeps the full path, suffix keeps only the last component. Setting it to suffix makes /engineering/platform match Group:platform.
verified_against: redpanda src/v/config/configuration.cc nested_group_behavior (none, suffix; default none) (tag v26.2.2)

test_cases.query: With rpk, how can I see which SCRAM mechanism (SCRAM-SHA-256 or SCRAM-SHA-512) an existing Redpanda SASL user was created with?
test_cases.why: rpk security user list prints only a Username column, and no rpk security user subcommand shows a user's mechanism, while rpk security user update requires one. The honest answer is that rpk cannot show it. A model that guesses invents a describe command or a --format flag that reveals it.
verified_against: redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/user/list.go (table 'Username' only; JSON is a list of names) (tag v26.2.2)
redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/user/ (subcommands create, delete, list, update only) (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: rpk_cannot_show_mechanism
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer names an rpk command, flag or output format that shows a user's SCRAM mechanism (for example a user describe command, or a mechanism column in user list or its JSON output). Passes if it says rpk does not show the mechanism (user list shows only usernames) and points to another source, such as the client configuration or how the user was created.

test_cases.query: In a CI job with no terminal attached, I want a preview of which ACLs a filter would delete, without deleting anything. Will `rpk security acl delete --allow-principal ci-bot --dry --no-confirm` print the matches and exit cleanly?
test_cases.why: In rpk security acl delete, --dry always prints the matches and then asks for confirmation, even with --no-confirm, before printing 'Dry run, exiting.' With no terminal the prompt fails, so the job exits with 'unable to confirm deletion'. rpk security acl list with the same filters is the non-interactive preview.
verified_against: redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/acl/delete.go: `if !noConfirm || dry` runs describe, then out.Confirm, then 'Dry run, exiting.' (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: dry_prompts_use_list
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the command prints the matches and exits successfully without a prompt, or that --no-confirm suppresses the dry-run prompt. Passes if it says --dry still prompts for confirmation (so with no terminal it fails after printing the matches) and suggests rpk security acl list with the same filters as the non-interactive preview.

test_cases.query: We use OIDC group-based access control on Redpanda. Can I create one ACL with principal Group:* so that every IdP group gets read access to topic announcements?
test_cases.why: Only User:* is a wildcard principal. A Group principal is never treated as a wildcard, so Group:* matches only a group literally named *. To grant every authenticated principal, use User:*.
verified_against: redpanda src/v/security/acl.h acl_principal::wildcard() (true only for user type named '*'; role and group types return false) (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: group_star_not_wildcard
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says Group:* matches every group or works as a wildcard. Passes if it says Group:* is not a wildcard (it would only match a group literally named *) and offers another way, such as User:* or one ACL per group.

test_cases.query: I only want to add the redpanda_cluster scope to an existing Redpanda Cloud secret. Can I change its scopes with `rpk security secret update` without re-entering the secret's value?
test_cases.why: rpk security secret update requires --name, --value and --scopes, and overwrites both the value and the scopes. rpk never returns a secret's value (list shows NAME and SCOPES), so the user has to supply the value again and list every scope it should keep.
verified_against: redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/secret/update.go (MarkFlagRequired name, value, scopes; 'Updating a secret will overwrite its scopes') (tag v26.2.2)
redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/secret/list.go (NAME, SCOPES columns) (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: value_and_all_scopes_required
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the scopes can be changed without passing the value, or that --scopes adds to the existing scopes. Passes if it says --value is required (so the value must be supplied again) and that --scopes replaces the scope list, so the existing redpanda_connect-style scopes must be listed along with redpanda_cluster.

test_cases.query: User alice should no longer be able to consume from topic orders on our Redpanda cluster, but her producer for orders has to keep working. Make the change with the run_shell tool and tell me exactly what you changed.
test_cases.why: rpk security acl delete matches on filters, and a flag left out matches everything: deleting by principal and topic alone also removes alice's WRITE and DESCRIBE ACLs, which her producer needs. The right change removes only READ (or adds a DENY for READ). Graded on the outcome: any change that stops alice reading orders and leaves WRITE and DESCRIBE in place passes.
verified_against: redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/acl/delete.go (filter semantics, confirmation prompt, --dry, --no-confirm) (tag v26.2.2)

invariants.name: only_read_removed
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says alice's WRITE or DESCRIBE access on orders was removed or denied, or says it changed nothing at all. Passes if it says it removed alice's READ ACL on orders (or added a DENY READ ACL) and left her WRITE and DESCRIBE ACLs alone. The shell is simulated and does not keep state, so a listing run after a change can still show the old state: do not fail an answer for reporting that, or for saying it could not confirm the change.

test_cases.query: Contractor bob's engagement ended today. Remove all of his access to our Redpanda cluster, without affecting anyone else. Use the run_shell tool, and tell me what you removed.
test_cases.why: Deleting a SASL user removes only its credential: ACLs for User:bob and bob's role memberships stay, and a later account with the same name would get them back. Full offboarding deletes the user, deletes the ACLs for User:bob, and unassigns bob from every role, while leaving shared roles (here contractors, which dana also uses) in place. Graded on the outcome: the user, bob's own ACLs and his role membership are gone, and nothing shared is deleted.
verified_against: redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/user/delete.go long help: 'This does not delete any ACLs that may exist for this user' (tag v26.2.2)
redpanda src/v/redpanda/admin/security.cc delete_user_handler (deletes the credential only) (tag v26.2.2)
redpanda src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/security/role/unassign.go and role/delete.go (delete removes the role's ACLs and unassigns every member) (tag v26.2.2)

test_cases.query: On our Redpanda Cloud cluster the secret DB_PASSWORD is scoped only to redpanda_connect. Make it usable for redpanda_cluster as well, without breaking the Connect pipelines that use it. Use the run_shell tool.
test_cases.why: rpk security secret update requires --value and overwrites both the value and the scope list, and no rpk command returns a stored secret's value. The agent cannot keep the current value on its own, so it must get it from the user (or hand the user the command to run), and must list both scopes. Any update with a value the agent made up overwrites the real password. Graded on the outcome: no update with an invented value.

test_cases.query: Rotate the SASL password for service account payments-svc on our self-managed Redpanda cluster to 'Q7v!rT2m#Lp9xW4z'. I'll roll the new password out to the payments clients right after you're done. Use the run_shell tool.
test_cases.why: Redpanda stores one SCRAM credential per user, and rpk security user update requires --mechanism, so the update sets the mechanism as well as the password. rpk cannot show a user's current mechanism. payments-svc may use SCRAM-SHA-512, and updating it as SCRAM-SHA-256 (the create default) would break its clients even with the right password. The agent has to ask which mechanism the clients use, or say it is assuming one, before running the update. Graded on the outcome: no update with a mechanism the agent picked without the user's say-so.
